title: Assessment of Groundwater Contamination Risk from ⁹⁰Sr in the Chornobyl Exclusion Zone Using Machine Learning, GIS Mapping, and Groundwater Modelling
content: Groundwater contamination by 90Sr remains an important component of the long-term environmental impact of the Chornobyl accident, while the spatial coverage of monitoring observations limits direct assessment of contamination patterns across the Chornobyl Exclusion Zone (CEZ). This study evaluates the applicability of machine-learning methods for regional assessment of 90Sr groundwater contamination and identification of its principal controlling factors. Random Forest (RF) and XGBoost models were developed using groundwater 90Sr observations for 2015-2020 and source-related, hydrogeological, geochemical, topographic, and monitoring-well predictors. Performance was evaluated using repeated stratified holdout validation for multiclass classification and complementary regression of log-transformed 90Sr concentrations. Regional contamination classes were subsequently predicted using spatially distributed predictor layers. The RF classifier, predicting order-of-magnitude concentration classes, achieved a mean accuracy of 0.70 and weighted F1-score of 0.66, compared with 0.64 and 0.62 for XGBoost, whereas XGBoost showed slightly higher regression performance (R2 = 0.55) than RF (R2= 0.50). Across model-specific, permutation and SHAP analyses, groundwater-table depth, aquifer sampling depth, and surface 90Sr contamination were repeatedly identified among the most influential predictors. Spatial predictions indicated that higher contamination classes were localized and primarily associated with the combination of elevated surface contamination and shallow groundwater conditions, with notable correspondence to radioactive-waste disposal areas. The results provide spatial information to support prioritization and development of groundwater monitoring networks in the CEZ.
